items.longBusinessSummary: Okta, Inc. operates as an identity partner in the United States and internationally. It offers Single Sign-on to secure access to cloud and on-premises applications from any device; Adaptive MFA for a risk-based layer of security for an organization's cloud, mobile, and web applications; API Access Management, which enables organizations to secure APIs as systems; Access Gateway, which extends the Okta platform to hybrid IT environments; Okta Device Access, which extends Okta platform's secure access management to the device login experience; Universal Directory for a cloud-based system of record. The company also provides Identity Threat Protection; Identity Security Posture Management for security measures and safeguards digital assets; Okta for AI Agents to discover, register, authenticate, govern, and manage AI Agents; Identity Governance and Administration products, including Lifecycle Management, Okta Workflows, Okta Identity Governance, and Cross App Access; Advanced Server Access for continuous and contextual access management to secure cloud infrastructure; and Okta Privileged Access to reduce risk with unified access and governance management. In addition, it provides Universal Login, a standards-based login infrastructure; Attack Protection Suite to minimize risks associated with identity-targeted attacks; Adaptive MFA; Passwordless, which enables users to login without a password; Machine-to-Machine Tokens for authentication and authorization with NHIs; Private Cloud, a deployment option; Organizations, which support a large number of partners or customers; Extensibility, which enables customers to build customized identity flows; Fine Grained Authorization, which manages complex authorization scenarios; and Auth0 for AI Agents to secure and scale agentic applications. The company was formerly known as Saasure, Inc. Okta, Inc. was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

Item 5.02 Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers.
Departure of Director; Appointment of New Director
On September 14, 2026, Emilie Choi, a Class I director of the Board of Directors (the “Board”) of Okta, Inc. (the “Company”), provided notice that she would resign from the Board, effective that day. Ms. Choi’s resignation is not the result of disagreement with the Company on any matters relating to its operations, policies or practices. The Board expresses its appreciation for Ms. Choi’s service to the Company and her invaluable contributions to the Board.
Additionally, on September 17, 2026, the Board, upon the recommendation of its Compensation and Corporate Governance Committee, appointed Helen Riley as an independent director of the Company, effective September 18, 2026. The Board appointed Ms. Riley as a Class I director, to serve until the Company’s 2027 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, and as a member of the Audit Committee of the Board (the “Audit Committee”). She will hold office until her successor has been duly elected and qualified, or until her earlier death, resignation or removal.
There are no arrangements or understandings between Ms. Riley and any other persons pursuant to which she was appointed as a director. There are no transactions between Ms. Riley and the Company that would be required to be reported under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.
Ms. Riley will participate in the Company’s standard non-employee director compensation arrangements. Under the terms of those arrangements, she will receive, among other things, annual compensation of $35,000 for her service on the Board, $13,000 for her service on the Audit Committee, and an initial grant of 2,907 restricted stock units that vest annually over three years, subject to continuous service.
The Company has entered into its standard form of indemnification agreement with Ms. Riley.
A copy of the press release announcing the appointment of Ms. Riley to the Board and departure of Ms. Choi from the Board is attached hereto as Exhibit 99.1.

Title: Why Did META, MRNA, OKTA Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today?
Author: Aashika Suresh   Thu, September 24, 2026 at 5:52 AM GMT+2 3 min read
Published: 2026-09-24T03:52:46+00:00
=== BODY ===
META stock gained about 1% at close after it revealed new products at its annual two-day Connect event on Wednesday.
MRNA stock rose higher during trading hours but closed down 0.25% after the CEO said it was more an 'mRNA platform company' than a vaccine firm.
OKTA stock jumped more than 4% as investor optimism over autonomous AI agents continued to grow.
Shares of Meta Platforms Inc. (META), Moderna Inc. (MRNA), and Okta Inc. (OKTA) rallied to fresh 52-week highs on Wednesday as new launches, positive management commentary, and rising investor optimism bolstered them higher.
META stock gained about 1% at close after it revealed new products at its annual two-day Connect event on Wednesday.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
MRNA stock rose higher during trading hours but closed down 0.25% after the CEO said it was more an 'mRNA platform company' than a vaccine firm.
OKTA stock jumped more than 4% as investor optimism over autonomous AI agents continued to grow.
META stock hit a 52-week high of $763.90 on Wednesday, putting it on track for a fifth consecutive week of gains.
At its latest event, Meta Connect 2026, the company debuted its Meta VR Glasses and the AI-powered Muse Charm, a pocket-sized, keychain-friendly standalone hardware device. Meta also launched a range of new Meta Ray-Ban Glasses.
The Mark Zuckerberg-led company revealed Ray-Ban Meta Audio, its first pair of Ray-Ban smart glasses without a camera, equipped with a 12MP camera, up to nine hours of battery life, a customizable action button and new Aviator and Zena frames. Meta also added Capri and Nova styles to its own Meta Glasses line.
Meta's Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared feature for adults with mild-to-moderate hearing loss, also garnered eyeballs.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around META stock was 'bullish' at the time of writing. The company's shares have climbed more than 14% so far this year.
MRNA stock rose to a fresh 52-week high of $192.31 on Wednesday after CEO Stéphane Bancel said at the Bernstein Insights: Healthcare Leaders and Disruptors 3rd Annual Healthcare Forum that the company "has never been" a COVID-19 vaccine company, but rather is an mRNA platform company.
According to The Fly, Bancel said Moderna's mRNA is a technology that can be used to develop treatments across multiple diseases, not just vaccines.
Chief Development Officer David Berman added that the company is now focused on three main areas: vaccines, oncology and rare diseases.
The comments come as Moderna is seeking to prove the potential of mRNA beyond infectious diseases, particularly in cancer.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MRNA stock was 'bullish' at the time of writing. The stock has jumped more than 490% year to date.
OKTA stock climbed to an annual high of $207.20 on Wednesday, notching three consecutive days of gains.
Surging enterprise demand for securing autonomous AI agents has fueled optimism around the stock, with investors eyeing a further leg up.
Shares have also gained attention in recent weeks after a blowout fiscal second-quarter 2027 report, in which the company raised full-year guidance.
For FY27, the company guided to $3.216 billion to $3.226 billion in revenue, indicating 10%–11% growth and a 26% non-GAAP operating margin.
Meanwhile, earlier this week, Baird raised its price target on Okta to $200 from $185 and maintained an 'Outperform' rating on the shares, along with a preview of Oktane'26, Okta's annual flagship conference, scheduled for this week in Las Vegas, Nevada.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around OKTA stock improved to 'bullish' from 'bearish'. The company's shares have surged about 145% year to date.

Title: Okta Sees AI Agent Identity Market Outgrowing Traditional IAM at Oktane 2026
Author: MarketBeat   Wed, September 23, 2026 at 11:02 PM GMT+2 6 min read
Published: 2026-09-23T21:02:08+00:00
=== BODY ===
Interested in Okta, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.
Okta sees AI-agent identity as a major long-term opportunity that could eventually surpass the traditional identity and access management market, with market leadership likely established over the next three years.
The company is promoting an open ecosystem through its Blueprint Alliance and Cross App Access protocol, while expanding Agent SSO and support for third-party providers such as Microsoft Entra ID to drive interoperability and future upgrades.
AI-agent adoption remains early, but Okta reports meaningful initial deal contributions and expects pricing to shift from user-based models toward agent-based pricing as autonomous workflows become more common.
Securing AI: 5 Most-Upgraded Stocks From the Q2 Reporting Season
Okta (NASDAQ:OKTA) executives said the company is positioning its identity platform to play a central role in securing and governing artificial intelligence agents, arguing that the emerging "agentic" technology market could ultimately exceed the size of today's identity and access management market.
Speaking at the company's Investor Summit at Oktane 2026, Co-Founder and CEO Todd McKinnon said AI agents are driving changes across the technology stack and will require new approaches to identity, governance, visibility and security. He described the shift as a long-term opportunity, while acknowledging that adoption will take time and competition will intensify.
→ These 3 AI Stocks Sold Off Hard—Even as Their Outlooks Improved
Okta Stock Surges 29%—Is $200 the Next Stop?
"The market share established over the next three years for the agent, call it the system of record for agent identities, is going to play out over the next three years," McKinnon said. "There is going to be massive growth and the market share is going to be set probably in three years."
McKinnon discussed the company's Blueprint Alliance, an industry effort intended to bring more clarity to the security architecture needed for AI agents. He said the initiative is designed to help customers distinguish between functions such as AI gateways, MCP gateways, risk management and governance, rather than forcing customers to make decisions amid a fragmented vendor landscape.
→ Insiders Signal Deep Value In DICK's Sporting Goods
5 Stocks to Buy in September Before Wall Street Catches On
According to McKinnon, the alliance's goal is to "make the pie bigger for everyone" by encouraging interoperability and providing customers with a framework for deploying secure agentic systems. He said the next phase will depend on customer adoption and endorsement, followed by work with alliance partners to validate that products operate together within a reference architecture.
While analysts raised the prospect of joint go-to-market arrangements and economic incentives among alliance members, McKinnon said those efforts would be premature before customer traction and technical integration are established.
→ Coach's Momentum Powers Tapestry Despite the Stock's Sharp Pullback
He also highlighted Cross App Access, described as an open protocol for enabling agents to securely access applications. Okta is making its Agent SSO capability broadly available across its products to encourage independent software vendors to support the protocol. McKinnon said the company expects broader adoption of the protocol to create a path toward paid upgrades to Okta for AI Agents, which provides additional lifecycle management, governance and connection capabilities.
Okta executives said support for third-party identity providers is an important part of their strategy, particularly for customers using Microsoft Entra ID. McKinnon said many large organizations have Microsoft identity deployments but are seeking a more flexible platform for AI-agent use cases and connections with non-Microsoft technologies.
Ric Smith, Okta's President of Products and Technology, said the company is seeing growing demand to connect its offerings to independent identity providers. Okta plans to expand that approach across governance, privileged access management and the Auth0 platform, he said.
McKinnon said AI-related discussions can lead to broader platform deployments, including workforce identity, governance, privilege management and customer identity capabilities. Jon Addison, Okta's Chief Revenue Officer, said the company's specialized sales organization has helped AI conversations reach a broad set of stakeholders, including CIOs, CISOs and teams responsible for external-facing applications.
Addison said spending on agentic security is still typically sourced from traditional CIO and CISO budgets, though the company is increasingly seeing R&D and engineering budgets support external-facing agent initiatives. McKinnon said approximately 80% of his current AI-agent discussions remain with IT and security buyers, but he expects more involvement from business-oriented leaders, such as chief digital officers, as customer-facing agent use cases develop.
For Okta for AI Agents, McKinnon said pricing currently is generally tied to users because many early deployments are intended to improve the productivity of individual employees. He said pricing is likely to evolve toward an agent-based model as workflows become more autonomous, though the industry has not yet developed a standard way to count agents.
Using round numbers, McKinnon said certain sizable deals have included AI-agent spending of roughly 1 to 1.5 against an overall Okta platform spend of 4. He said that implies an uplift comparable to, or potentially greater than, the company has seen with Okta Identity Governance attachments, while cautioning that the sample size remains small.
Addison said Okta has revised its sales methodology for AI and invested in tools, specialized teams and partner relationships to address customers' varied maturity levels and use cases. He said partners co-sold the company's top 20 deals in the second quarter, and Okta's largest deal in that period was partner sourced.
McKinnon said organizations adopting Okta for AI Agents are generally already pursuing agentic capabilities through third-party platforms or internal development efforts. He cited companies including Ramp, Yahoo and Dell as examples of businesses that see potential in agents and are moving forward with deployments.
He characterized current adopters as early adopters and said wider adoption may take longer than expected, but could ultimately be larger than anticipated. Comparing the opportunity with the demand catalyst created by the COVID-19 pandemic, McKinnon said the agentic transition "feels way bigger" because it represents a new technology shift rather than the culmination of an existing move toward identity-centric security.
In public sector markets, Addison said agentic deployments remain early, though the company has seen strong broader public-sector performance following investments in regulated environments, including FedRAMP High and IL5. McKinnon added that large government agencies are pursuing pilots and prototypes for Okta for AI Agents, with compliance readiness across the platform remaining a key requirement for deployment.
Okta, Inc provides cloud-based identity and access management solutions for organizations. Its platform helps businesses securely connect employees, customers, partners and applications while managing authentication, authorization and user access across cloud, on-premises and mobile environments.
The company's offerings include single sign-on, multifactor authentication, adaptive access controls, lifecycle management, identity governance and privileged access capabilities. Through its Customer Identity Cloud, powered by Auth0, Okta also provides tools for developers and businesses to embed authentication and authorization features into applications and digital services.
Founded in 2009 by Todd McKinnon and Frederic Kerrest, Okta completed its initial public offering in 2017.
